title: Rollout health canvas and 24h watchlist
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick, scannable canvas for the first 24 hours after a release.
- Focus: operational signals + lowest-effort mitigations so on-call and release operators can act fast.
- Not the canonical runbook (that lives in Confluence -> CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-3312). This is the compact, dirty 24h watchlist we actually stick on the war-room whiteboard.

Goals:
- Detect regressions in latency/cost/accuracy within 30 minutes of first traffic shift.
- Ramp to target traffic safely or rollback within 60 minutes if thresholds trigger.
- Keep customer-facing error surface <= 0.5% during rollout.

Quick summary (one-line for slack / pager):
- Release: feature/optimize-routing v2026.05.04
- Canary start: 2026-05-12 09:00 UTC -> initial 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (see cadence below)
- Owners on deck: Aisha (release lead), Marcus (telemetry & alerts), Elena (canary + infra), Priya (observability), Tom (rollback lead)

Preflight checklist (do not skip):
- [ ] Smoke builds green: CI pipeline 1/2/3 green -> link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release/actions
- [ ] Canary config reviewed in PR 482 and approved by infra and SRE
- [ ] Baseline metrics snapshot taken (latency P50/P90/P99, error rate, token cost) -> attach snapshot to CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-3312
- [ ] Load tests: 30m synthetic at 110% expected canary QPS -> pass SLA for keyed endpoints
- [ ] DB migrations checked and feature-flag guards in place
- [ ] Canary routing fallback path verified (route->fallback-model)
- [ ] Slack channel #release-runway set and all owners invited
- [ ] Pager rota for 24h watch assigned in schedule doc

Canary cadence (annotated):
- 09:00 UTC: 2% traffic for 20 minutes (fast smoke) -> manual decision point
  - quick checks: 5m latency, 10m error rate, 20m cost burn compared to baseline
- 09:20 UTC: if stable -> 10% traffic for 40 minutes (observational)
  - checks: rolling P99, KV cache hit-rate, memory usage per GPU, unexpected OOMs
- 10:00 UTC: if stable -> 50% traffic for 60 minutes (stress observation)
  - checks: throughput backpressure, queueing, tail-latency spikes under load
- 11:00 UTC: if stable -> 100% gradual shift over 30 minutes
  - post-shift monitoring for 3 hours intensively (see watchlist)

Health signals and thresholds (auto-trigger / manual decision):
- Latency P99 increase > 30% vs baseline for two consecutive windows -> issue alert to SRE and consider rollback
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes -> auto-alert + pause ramp
- Cost per 1k tokens increases > 25% with no QoL improvement -> hold and investigate
- KV cache hit-rate drop > 10% -> inspection of routing mismatch or model variant mismatch
- GPU mem OOMs / process restarts: immediate rollback criteria
- Accuracy/regression signals from eval-suite: any failing regression test -> pause

Primary instrumentation to watch (dash links left intentionally short):
- Latency dashboard: latency.p50/p90/p99 (prod)
- Errors: http.5xx, model-inference.errors
- Throughput: tokens/s, requests/s, queue-length
- Cost breakdown: token-costs-per-route, gpu-utilization, model-variant-cost
- Model quality: regression set pass-rate, random-sample review queue
- Telemetry: sample traces for any P99 anomalies (attach trace IDs to incident)

Operator runbook (first 30m):
1) On slack channel, post current step and baseline snapshot.
2) Watch live dashboard (Priya) and call out anomalous signals.
3) If threshold breached: Marcus to triage telemetry, Elena to inspect infra metrics, Tom to prepare rollback patch.
4) If rollback needed: follow rollback checklist below and open JIRA ticket JIRA-REL-8901 with "rollback-executed" label.

Rollback checklist (fast path):
- [ ] Pause traffic ramp immediately (console: route-control -> pause-ramp)
- [ ] Failover routes to stable model variant (route-policy -> stable)
- [ ] Revert deployment in kube (kubectl rollout undo deployment/release-proxy) or revert PR 482 via GitHub if needed
- [ ] Clear cache where appropriate or reset prefix KV cache (if cache poisoning suspected)
- [ ] Notify customers if rollout touched > 1% of active users via status page draft
- [ ] Postmortem tag + on-call assignment

Low-friction mitigations (try before rollback for non-critical warnings):
- Reduce batch size or throttle concurrency for affected route for 15 minutes
- Switch to lower-cost quantized variant if mem pressure is the issue
- Enable short-lived circuit-breaker to shed low-priority requests
- Temporarily route heavy traffic to Dedicated tier if overload is infra-limited

24-hour watchlist (what to re-check every 30–60 minutes):
- Latency P50/P90/P99 (compare to baseline snapshot)
- 5xx error rate and service-specific error counters
- Token cost per route and unexpected cost spikes
- Any new customer tickets on support triage board mentioning generation latency/regressions
- Autoscaler events and pod restarts (SRE)
- Sample 5 random successful and 5 failed responses for correctness review
- Regression eval-run results (every 2 hours for the first 8 hours)

Communication playbook (who to ping and when):
- If mild anomaly (non-blocking): notify #release-runway and tag owners
- If service-impacting: open Slack huddle + call (Aisha) and page SRE primary
- If rollback executed: brief execs via email (template in CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-3312) and update status page

Post-release notes (to fill out after 24h):
- Traffic ramp timeline with timestamps and decision notes
- Any mitigations performed and their short-term outcome
- Post-24h metrics snapshot (latency, error rate, cost)
- Customer impact summary and support tickets opened/closed
- Root cause/observations if rollback was necessary
- Follow-up TODOs and owners for next 7 days (regression tests, infra fixes, telemetry tweaks)

Open questions / TODOs for this template:
- Do we want an automated canary pause on certain ML-quality regressions? (Marcus to prototype)
- Add a lightweight pager message template for rapid exec notification (Aisha)
- Confirm that Dedicated-tier quick-routing is available as temporary mitigation across regions (Elena)

Notes to self / quick scribbles:
- Keep the 2% initial window long enough to collect useful P99 traces (20m felt OK last sprint).
- Watch for pattern where P99 jumps but user-facing error rate stays low — often a cold-KV miss or new kernel path causing tail latency.
- If noisy signal, reduce sampling window rather than flip rollout.

Attachments and artifacts to copy here after release (postmortem skeleton):
- Final ramp timestamps and decision rationale (text)
- Graph snapshots (latency/error/cost) attached as PNGs
- Jira ticket links for any follow-ups
- Annotated sample traces for any P99 anomalies

Bottom line: this canvas is the smallest useful artifact the ops team needs to run the first 24 hours of a rollout with low friction. Use it in the war-room, iterate after each release.

---
Document history:
- 2026-05-04: initial draft by Aisha
- 2026-05-08: telemetry thresholds adjusted (Marcus)
- 2026-05-12: cadence and owners finalized for v2026.05.04

Quick links referenced in doc:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-3312
- Jira: JIRA-REL-8901
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release/pull/482

End.
